title: Habitual grace includes infused virtues and justifying grace
source_text: XX. Jam autem sub gratia habituali comprehendunt omnes habitus virtutum infusos, ac praesertim gratiam illam in qua consistere volunt justitiam per quam formaliter coram Deo justificamur: quae ab iis dicitur Gratia justificans, & plerumque Gratia simpliciter & sine addito: & ad quam in communi usu, gratiae gratum facientis nomen restringi solet.
pass_a_gloss: XX. Now under habitual grace they comprehend all the infused habits of virtues, and especially that grace in which they will to consist the righteousness by which formally we are justified before God: which by them is called justifying Grace, and mostly Grace simply and without addition: and to which in common use, the name of grace making pleasing is wont to be restricted.
pass_b_english: Thesis XX. Under habitual grace they include all the infused habits of the virtues, and above all the grace in which, on their view, consists the righteousness by which we are formally justified before God.
They call this justifying grace, and usually just 'grace' with nothing added, and in common usage the name 'grace that makes pleasing' is usually confined to it.

lemmas.gloss: all the infused habits of virtues

lemmas.latin: justitiam per quam formaliter coram Deo justificamur
lemmas.gloss: the righteousness by which formally we are justified before God

choices.why: Scholastic: the righteousness that is the form of the justified man, inherent rather than imputed; this is the point Protestants contest.
